figA_gain3d: Paired improvement of the refined two-stage stochastic policy over the baseline pipeline across all case × mapping cells (CRN-synchronized trials; 30 seeds per cell). Gains are uniformly non-negative and are largest in the S2/S3 hard cases.
figB_waterfall: Ablation ledger from the deterministic dispatch baseline to the final two-stage stochastic policy. Every upgrade is evaluated as a paired contrast on the same 450 validation trials (common random numbers); bars show the incremental gain with 95% CI.
figG_paired_dist: Distribution of the 150 trial-level paired gains behind Figure 12 (grey points, jittered; 5 mappings × 30 seeds per case). The mean ± 95% CI (blue diamonds) sits above zero in every case: the gain is carried by the bulk of trials, not by a handful of outliers.
figC1_r2: Out-of-sample R² of prefix-based duration prediction for three prefix windows and three estimators. All values are negative: even the best gradient-boosting model cannot beat the family-mean guess, and the ridge estimator the baseline relied on is the worst (*).
figC2_falsified: Mean cost per trial (blue/red, left axis) and reviews bought per trial (amber/grey, right axis) for the falsified information route — an adversarial arm allowed to buy the maximum number of reviews — versus the refined zero-review policy. The falsified route pays +4.64 more per trial and still loses on timeliness (Figure 16).
figC3_adversarial: Paired gain of the adversarial buy-top arm against the refined zero-review policy on validation (mean ± 95% CI, 450 paired trials). Even with every informational advantage, the buying arm is significantly worse, closing the information-layer question.
figH_duration_model: Fitted hierarchical log-normal duration model (σ floored at 0.35 to avoid overconfident tails from small samples). Family A is short and tight; family L is heavy-tailed — the source of most censoring events — and drives the robust-anchor design choice.
figD_censoring: Truncation handling against a known-truth simulation (500 repeats, right-censoring at the median). Dropping censored jobs — the baseline practice — biases log-mean estimates by about −0.6; the EM censoring-aware update brings the bias to ≈0, protecting every downstream scheduling decision.
figE_saa: Sample-average-approximation bounds for the deployed policy class at the nominal mapping. The lower bound (blue, with 95% CI) is exact for S1 by enumeration; candidate sequences fall inside the confidence interval, so the relative optimality gap is reported as zero (local search bound for S2/S3, flagged with a caveat).
figF_generalization: Main contrast (refined online policy vs the strongest naive WSPT variant) on validation seeds and on independent test seeds. The gain replicates out-of-sample, confirming that it reflects model design rather than seed luck.
